title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for liver metastases.

HPI
The patient is a 66-year-old male presenting for a follow-up evaluation regarding his history of prostate cancer. He had his primary carcinoma removed and underwent treatment several years ago. He reports that his treatment is complete and he feels well currently. He is here today specifically to address the development of liver metastases. He denies any new systemic symptoms or localized pain.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. He appears in no acute distress. Abdomen is soft and non-tender without palpable masses. Vital signs are stable and within normal limits.

Assessment
1. Liver metastases: The patient presents with metastatic disease to the liver. We will monitor his liver function and symptoms closely.
2. Prostate cancer: The primary site shows no evidence of local recurrence. Treatment of the primary site is complete and no further intervention is indicated at that location.

Plan
1. Liver metastases: Schedule a follow-up imaging study to monitor the progression of the liver involvement.
2. Prostate cancer: Continue current observation; no active treatment is required for the primary site.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: The prostate cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.46 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
